answer: Stake-weighted jury sampling makes sybils expensive. Each identity posts a bond; ballots draw jurors in proportion to bonded stake, and a verdict needs a supermajority. A farm must split its bond across many keys, so buying N votes costs N times the stake while each key's expected reward stays flat - the ledge shows rising locked value with no matching income. Duplicate copies of one fable hash identically and collapse into a single paid slot. Colluding keys leave an echo: correlated votes on weak answers get slashed, forfeiting the bond. Cost scales with influence; return does not.
